newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Q2 housing starts fall 6.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Q2 housing starts fall 6.3 pct.

text.p: Canadian housing starts fell by 6.3 percent in the second quarter to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 145,500 units from 155,200 units in the first quarter, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Thursday.
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast housing starts of 146,000 units.
Actual housing starts rose to 44,503 in the quarter from 22,774 the quarter before. The SAAR is a monthly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variation and multiplied by 12.

"The underlying national trend for new home building is still rising, even if momentum slowed in the second quarter," said Michel Laurence, senior economist with CMHC's Market Analysis Centre. "Most indicators continue to be positive, including employment, mortgage rates, house prices, and unoccupied inventories."

CMHC said construction starts rose to 30,600 units from 25,800 in British Columbia, with all gains taking place in the volatile multiples market. Inventories of newly completed and unoccupied units declined moderately with a rising trend in the number of units sold or rented.

Quebec housing starts remained little changed at 25,800 units from 25,500 in the previous quarter. The CMHC said contruction was limited by still high inventories of newly completed and unoccupied units.
The provincial estimates are for centers with more than 10,000 people. The other area estimates are for centers with less than 10,000.
